page.title: Best 3D Scanner That Works With a Phone (2026): Tested Picks by Phone and Budget
page.h1: Best 3D scanner that works with a phone
page.desc: The Creality Pika scans from a recent iPhone or flagship Android with a 0.03 mm blue laser, a 260 g body and two batteries. Check your phone's chip first. Budget and no-phone picks inside.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 3D scanner that works with a phone is the Creality Pika ({buy:creality-pika-3d-scanner}): a 260 g scanner with a 7-line blue laser rated to 0.03 mm, a built-in touchscreen, and two swappable batteries (up to 70 minutes each) in the box. Check your phone first, because that is where phone scanning most often fails. The Pika needs at least an iPhone with an A15 chip and 6 GB of RAM, or an Android phone with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 and 8 GB. On mid-range phones, owners report 1 to 3 frames per second and no laser mode at all.

On a phone, the Pika's laser mode needs the marker towers or dots in the box. Creality says marker-free laser scanning works only when the scanner is wired to a PC. If your phone is older or your budget is under $400, the Creality CR-Scan Ferret Pro ({buy:creality-cr-scan-ferret-pro}) comes with a battery handle and wireless bridge. It is rated to 0.1 mm for objects from 6 in to 6.5 ft. If you want to scan with no phone and no computer, the Revopoint MIRACO ($1,274 on Revopoint's store, seen 2026-11-17) scans and processes on its own screen.

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Lost tracking and markers (7 mentions in the reviews and threads we read). Every scanner here struggles with symmetric, featureless, black, shiny or clear objects. Plan on marker dots or a vanishing scanning spray. The Pika's laser mode on a phone needs markers. The Ferret Pro needs spray on dark or translucent parts.
  • The phone or PC is too weak (5). On a Snapdragon 695 phone, the Pika's laser captured nothing and NIR ran at about 1 fps. Owners with a Dimensity 900 and a Galaxy A55 got about 3 fps and no laser mode. A Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 or newer phone ran every mode. The Revopoint POP 4's recommended PC calls for a high-end Nvidia graphics card.
  • Rough software (4). Owners call Creality Scan usable but rough in places. Ferret Pro reviews often say "glitchy". The POP 4 phone app was in beta at launch.
  • Batteries (3). Pika test units arrived with flat batteries and would not start on USB power alone. One Ferret Pro reviewer says its handle battery drains quickly.
  • Hair (2). Reviewers say hair stays hard to capture with the Pika in every mode.

Which one by need

  • Small, detailed parts from a recent phone: Creality Pika. It is the only one here with a screen and two batteries in the box, and its laser is rated to 0.03 mm.
  • Older phone, bigger objects, under $400: Creality CR-Scan Ferret Pro. It covers 6 in to 6.5 ft and comes with a handle and wireless bridge.
  • Finer detail than the Ferret Pro on a budget: Revopoint INSPIRE 2, rated to 0.05 mm. Add the Mobile Kit if you want to scan without a cord.
  • No phone and no computer: Revopoint MIRACO, which does the scanning and processing on the device.

Not recommended

  • The Pika on a mid-range phone. Below a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, or an iPhone older than the A15 chip with 6 GB of RAM, owners report no laser mode and 1 to 3 fps.
  • The Revopoint POP 4 if a phone is all you have. It is built around a strong Nvidia PC, its phone app launched in beta, and cordless use needs the $111 Mobile Kit.
